_meta.standard: IEEE C57.91 (Guide for loading mineral-oil-immersed transformers), Clause 7 exponential thermal model and the insulation aging clauses
_meta.edition: C57.91-2011 as cited by the secondary sources below (C57.91-2025 is now the active edition; its revised Clause 7 model is not implemented here)
_meta.note: The licensed standard was not read. Every value below comes from public secondary sources (an open-access paper, a journal paper and IEEE Transformers Committee slides) that cite C57.91. Nothing here may be set to VERIFIED until it is checked against a licensed copy. Transformer-specific values (rated rises, loss ratio R, time constants) are NOT stored as defaults: they are inputs taken from the unit's test report. The only preset is an illustrative parameter set published for one real 25 MVA ONAF unit.

sources.arxiv_1703_01397: Majzoobi, Mahoor, Khodaei, 'Machine Learning Applications in Estimating Transformer Loss of Life', arXiv:1703.01397 (2017), Section II eqs. 1-11, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01397
sources.gouda_2012: Gouda, Amer, Salem, 'Predicting transformer temperature rise and loss of life in the presence of harmonic load currents', Ain Shams Engineering Journal (2012), doi:10.1016/j.asej.2012.01.003, Section 2 and Table 2
sources.roizman_2021: O. Roizman, 'Loading Guide C57.91 New Clause 7 and Annex A', IEEE PES Transformers Committee, Insulation Life SC, 16 Nov 2021, https://grouper.ieee.org/groups/transformers/subcommittees/insulation_life/c57.91/F21-PC57.91-OlegRoizman-Clause7,AnnexA.pdf

aging.insulation: thermally upgraded paper, 65 C average winding rise basis
aging.clause: C57.91 aging acceleration factor (Clause 5 as cited)
aging.source: arxiv_1703_01397 eq. 2 (B = 15000 chosen in C57.91-2011, reference 110 C = 383 K); gouda_2012 eq. for F_AA

normal_life_h.basis: C57.91 normal insulation life (end-point as used for distribution transformers); the guide lets the user choose another end-point
normal_life_h.source: arxiv_1703_01397 Section II (180 000 h per C57.91-2011); gouda_2012 Section 5 (180 000 h, 20.6 years); roizman_2021 slide 'Proposed definitions (con't)' (180 000 h minimum life expectancy)

exponents._note: n = oil exponent (top-oil rise), m = winding exponent (hot-spot gradient). The secondary sources give only the range 0.8 to 1.0 by cooling mode (C57.91 Table 4 as cited by arxiv_1703_01397), n = 0.8 for natural convection and 0.9 to 1.0 for forced cooling, and m typically 0.8 (gouda_2012). The per-mode split for OFAF and ODAF below is recalled, not read; it lies inside the published range. Editable in the UI; test-derived exponents should be used when known.

ONAN.source: gouda_2012 Section 2 (n = 0.8 natural convection; m typical 0.8); arxiv_1703_01397 (range 0.8-1.0, C57.91 Table 4)

ONAF.source: gouda_2012 Table 2 (25 MVA ONAF unit: n = 0.9, m = 0.8) and Section 2 (n = 0.9-1.0 forced cooling)

OFAF.source: Recalled C57.91 Table 4 (non-directed forced oil); inside the 0.8-1.0 range of arxiv_1703_01397 and the forced-cooling n range of gouda_2012

ODAF.source: Recalled C57.91 Table 4 (directed forced oil); inside the 0.8-1.0 range of arxiv_1703_01397. Note: IEEE committee minutes (2004) report that the Clause 7 equations do not cover ODAF designs well.

gouda_2012_onaf_25mva.label: Illustrative only: 25 MVA ONAF unit (Gouda et al. 2012, Table 2)
gouda_2012_onaf_25mva.source: gouda_2012 Table 2 (rated top-oil rise 38.3 C, rated hot-spot rise over top oil 23.5 C, R = 5, top-oil time constant 114 min, hot-spot time constant 7 min, n = 0.9, m = 0.8). These are the published values for ONE 25 MVA, 66/11 kV unit, not typical values for any other transformer: replace them with the test-report values of the unit studied.
